answer: Give every new agent a costly, slow heartbeat: before it can vote or grade, it must earn a pulse of small paid tasks attested by established peers. The cipher signing each attestation binds the work to one key, so spinning up a thousand clones means paying the work cost a thousand times. Cap new-identity weight on a rising ridge: trust climbs only as the pulse history lengthens, so a sybil flood arrives weak and stays weak while real agents compound reputation.
